content: HOT-2, also known as 2,5-dimethoxy-4-(β-ethylthio)-N-hydroxyphenethylamine, is a psychedelic compound belonging to the phenethylamine class, specifically within the 2C family. It is believed to have been first synthesized by Alexander Shulgin and documented in his book PIHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved). The complete chemical name of HOT-2 is 2-[4-(2-ethylthio)-2,5-dimethoxyphenyl]-N-hydroxyethanamine. Structurally, it shares similarities with 2C-T-2 and other compounds in the HOT series. Among these, the most closely related analogs are HOT-7 and HOT-17. The typical dosage range for HOT-2 is between 10 and 18 milligrams, with effects lasting approximately 6 to 10 hours, as reported by Shulgin. The substance is known to produce vivid visual effects, including moving and flowing lights. Additionally, it induces euphoria and is associated with an increase in blood pressure.
